''6. Not man {{ls}}eparate.''] This in{{ls}}eparability betwixt man and wife ri{{ls}}eth of that, that wedlocke is a Sacrament. ''Aug. li. 2. de pec. origine c. 34. to. 7. De nupt. & concupi{{ls}}. li. 1. c. 10''.

''9. But for fornication.''] For aduoutrie one may dimi{{ls}}se an ''other, Mat. 5''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Mariage after diuorce vnlawful.}}But neither party can marry againe for any cau{{ls}}e during life. ''Aug. li. 11. de adult. coniug. c. 21. 22. 24''. for the which vnlawful act of marrying agayne, Fabiola that noble matrone of Rome albeit {{ls}}hee was the innocent part, did publike penance, as S. Hierom {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''In Epitaph. Fabiola.''}}writeth in her high commendation therefore. And in S. Paul ''Ro. 7''. it is plaine that {{ls}}hee which is with an other man, her hu{{ls}}band yet liuing, {{ls}}hal be called an aduoutere{{ls}}{{ls}}e: contrary to the doctrine of our Aduer{{ls}}aries.

''11. Not al take.''] Who{{ls}}oeuer haue not this gift geuen them, it is either for that they wil not haue it, or for that they fulfil not that which they wil: and they that haue this gift or attayne to this word, haue it of God and their owne free wil. ''Aug. li. de grat. & lib. arbit. c. 4''. So that it is euident no man is excluded from this gift, but (as Origen {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Orig. tract. 7. in Mat''.}}here {{ls}}aith) it is geuen to al that a{{ls}}ke for it: contrarie to our Aduer{{ls}}aries that {{ls}}ay it is impo{{ls}}sible, and that for excu{{ls}}e of breaking their vowes, wickedly {{ls}}ay, they haue not the gift.

''12. Gelded them {{ls}}elues.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Vow of cha{{ls}}titie.}}They geld them {{ls}}elues for the kingdom of heauen which vow cha{{ls}}tity. ''Aug. de virginitate c. 24''. Which proueth tho{{ls}}e kind of vowes to be both lawful, and al{{ls}}o more meritorious, and more {{ls}}ure to obtaine life euerla{{ls}}ting, then the {{ls}}tate of wedlocke. contrarie to our Adu. in al re{{ls}}pectes.

''12. He that can.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Coun{{ls}}els not Precepts.}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. {{ls}}er. 6. de temp.''}}It is not {{ls}}aid of the Precepts, keepe them who can, for they be nece{{ls}}sarie vnder paine of damnation to be kept: but of Coun{{ls}}els only (as of virginitie, ab{{ls}}taining from fle{{ls}}h and wine, and of geuing al a mans goods away to the poore) it is {{ls}}aid, He that can attaine to it, let him doe it: which is coun{{ls}}el only, not a commaundement. Contrary to our Adu. that {{ls}}ay, there are no Coun{{ls}}els, but only precepts.

''21. If thou wilt be perfect.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Religious {{ls}}tate of perfection.}}Loe, he maketh a plaine difference betwene keeping the commaundements, which is nece{{ls}}sary for euery man: and being perfect, which he coun{{ls}}eleth only to them that wil. And this is the {{ls}}tate of greate perfection which Religious men doe profe{{ls}}se, according to Chri{{ls}}tes coun{{ls}}el here, leauing al things and folowing him.

''21. Folow me.''] Thus to folow Chri{{ls}}t is to be without wife and care of children, to lacke propriety, and to liue in common, and this hath great reward in heauen aboue other {{ls}}tates of life: which, S. Augu{{ls}}tine {{ls}}aith, the Apo{{ls}}tles folowed, and him {{ls}}elf, and that he exhorted others to it as much as lay in him. ''Aug. ep. 89. in fine, & in p{{ls}}. 103 Conc. 3. po{{ls}}t med''.

''26. Al things po{{ls}}sible.''] This of the camel through a nedels eye, being po{{ls}}sible to God, although he neither hath done it, nor by like wil doe it: maketh again{{ls}}t the bla{{ls}}phemous infidelity of our Aduer{{ls}}aries that {{ls}}ay, God can do no more then he hath done or wil doe. We {{ls}}ee al{{ls}}o that God can bring a camel through a nedels eye, and therfore his body through a doore, and out of the {{ls}}epulchre {{ls}}hut, and out of his mother a virgin, and generally aboue nature and contrary to nature do with his body as he li{{ls}}t.

''27. Left al.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Vow of pouertie in re{{ls}}pect of reward.}}This perfection of leauing al things the Apo{{ls}}tles vowed. ''Aug. li. 17. de Ciu. Dei c. 4''.

''27. What {{ls}}hal we haue.''] They leaue al things in re{{ls}}pect of reward, and Chri{{ls}}t doeth wel allow it in them by his an{{ls}}wer.

''28. You al{{ls}}o {{ls}}hal {{ls}}itte.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. in p{{ls}}. 121.''}}Note that not only Chri{{ls}}t, who is the principal and proper iudge of the liuing and the dead, but with him the Apo{{ls}}tles and al perfect Saints {{ls}}hal iudge: and yet that doeth nothing derogate to his prerogatiue, by whom and vnder whom they hold this and al other dignities in this life and the next.<noinclude>{{rh|||CHAP.}}</noinclude>
